sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page suun1239 and reference pages 9216, 548879, 575531; IdRef/RAMEAU authority 15990577X 'Kisuundi (langue)'; SUDOC SRU; Harmathèque record.
sources.note: Catalogue records only: Glottolog lists exactly three descriptive refs (N'Landu 1994, Futi 2012, Nkombo 2014); SUDOC subject 'Kisuundi (langue)' returns only Futi 2012 and an unrelated popular book (Mouanga); RAMEAU variants Cisuundi/Kisoundi/Sundi/Suundi/Suundi de Kimongo.

sources.citation: Goes, Heidi & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Progressive vowel height harmony in Proto-Kikongo and Proto-Bantu. Journal of African Languages and Linguistics 40(1): 1-51.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Uses tone-marked Kisundi-Kimongo verb data from N'Landu 1994 (Appendix (38)) and Cisundi (Cabinda) data from Futi 2012 + 2018 fieldwork; p. 47 fn. 17 says the Kisundi-Kimongo variety (H131) 'straddles North Kikongo and West Kikongo'; treats Kisundi (Kimongo), Kisundi (Mboko-Songho) and Cisundi (Cabinda) as separate varieties (Table 3).

sources.citation: Bostoen, Koen & Gilles-Maurice de Schryver. 2018. Seventeenth-century Kikongo is not the ancestor of present-day Kikongo. In K. Bostoen & I. Brinkman (eds.), The Kongo Kingdom: The Origins, Dynamics and Cosmopolitan Culture of an African Polity, 60-102. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes 'Kisundi from Boko' (Congo-Brazzaville) fits Guthrie's H.16e Bwende slot and that Kisundi (Cabinda) and Cisundi datasets come from Goes's 2015 fieldwork.

sources.citation: de Schryver, Gilles-Maurice, Rebecca Grollemund, Simon Branford & Koen Bostoen. 2015. Introducing a state-of-the-art phylogenetic classification of the Kikongo Language Cluster. Africana Linguistica 21: 87-162.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Classification tables (pp. 103-104) separate Bastin's H13b Suundi (= Maho's H13b 'Sundi Kifouma') from H16i Suundi/Sundi (a Central Kongo/Manyanga dialect) — identity evidence only.

sources.citation: Bostoen, Koen, Odjas Ndonda Tshiyayi & Gilles-Maurice de Schryver. 2013. On the origin of the royal Kongo title ngangula. Africana Linguistica 19: 53-83.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gives Kisundi (Congo-Brazzaville) forms with lexical tone marks from Baka 1999 and Mabiala 1999 (kuháánà 'give'), and Cisundi (Cabinda) forms from Futi 2012: 32; lists the primary sources (Baka 1992/1999, Futi 2012, Mabiala 1999, Nkouanda 1997, Nsayi 1984).

sources.citation: Futi, João Maria. 2012. Essai de morphologie lexicale du cisuundi du Cabinda (Angola). Paris: L'Harmattan (IREA). 134 pp. ISBN 9782296960473 (e-PDF 9782296483743).

sources.note: The only full-length primary description of the Kimongo Kisuundi variety (Glottolog's top-ranked source); a 165-page 'éléments de description' will have a phonology chapter with tone and any accent/length statement. Its verb data are tone-marked (per Goes & Bostoen 2019 Appendix 38).

sources.citation: Goes, Heidi. 2022. A historical-comparative approach to phonological and morphological variation in the Kikongo Language Cluster with a special focus on Cabinda. PhD thesis, Ghent University.

sources.note: Comparative phonology of the Kikongo cluster with new Cabinda fieldwork (incl. Cisundi and Kisundi); its introduction may characterise prosody of the Cabinda varieties.

sources.note: Book unseen. From the open first page of Carter's 1976 review: it contains general phonological claims about 'Kongo' (a sequence of open syllables, p. 25; 'absence of consonant gemination'; a 'syllabic nasal'; placement of /v/ and /h/; vowels never in prefix-initial position, p. 67) alongside the nominal, verbal and nomino-verbal morphology, ideophones and proper names; whether tone is marked or analysed is not visible on p. 494, and p. 495 (where a Kongo tonologist reviewer would raise it) is paywalled. Worth a library check of its introduction/transcription section for a tone or accent stat…
